<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via /:name/runs/:runId/cancel (route, a path literal in a comment in handleAutomationRequest))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via /:name/runs/:runId/cancel (route, a path literal in a comment in handleAutomationRequest))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handleAutomationRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /:name/runs/:runId/cancel (route, a path literal in a comment in handleAutomationRequest))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **29** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a0e2d7767a5b95726872f671662cdd89f52c6aae` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bd36847f6b14e425a95678e833085e49bdd11314` — the merge of head `977833d6843c7c513c8131446af380d589e2b8e7` into base `a0e2d7767a5b95726872f671662cdd89f52c6aae`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bd36847f6b14e425a95678e833085e49bdd11314 && git checkout bd36847f6b14e425a95678e833085e49bdd11314
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a0e2d7767a5b95726872f671662cdd89f52c6aae 977833d6843c7c513c8131446af380d589e2b8e7 && git checkout -B drift-repro a0e2d7767a5b95726872f671662cdd89f52c6aae && git merge --no-ff 977833d6843c7c513c8131446af380d589e2b8e7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a0e2d7767a5b95726872f671662cdd89f52c6aae
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a0e2d7767a5b95726872f671662cdd89f52c6aae` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a7c8caddc54bbdf6c7b3759d92e58ec05cee9b6b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-addressed-route.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-run-lifecycle-door.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/automation-every-verb.hono.integration.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts

Face: narrowing. Inputs: card #32026 with all six comments, the PR body, file list and net diff against `main`, and the 56 check-runs on this head (37 success, 19 skipped by selector, 0 failed, 0 pending). Read and not reviewed: `domains/automation-address.ts`, `dispatcher-plugin.ts`, `packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set of `POST /automation/trigger/…`: narrowed, right.** Served after the change: `trigger/:name`, and `trigger/:ns/:name` where `:ns` is `_env` or an installed namespace. Declined: every `POST` whose parts, after the address read, number three or more. The three-part case was already declined by part (c). The new members of the declined set are four parts and deeper.
- **Answer on the mounted host: right.** The deep `POST` mounts a `trigger/…` path matches by parameter are `/:name/runs/:runId/resume|cancel|restore-suspension` (`:name` = `trigger`) and `/:ns/:name/runs/:runId/…` (`:ns` = `trigger`). Both now reach the decline, and the dispatcher answers `404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`. `Test Core` is green on the socket pins.
- **Answer on the catch-all host: right.** `dispatch()` returns `handled: false`, and `createHonoApp` answers an unhandled dispatch with its own `404` (`adapters/hono/src/index.ts:883`).
- **Other verbs: unchanged, right.** The condition keeps `m === 'POST'`. `GET trigger/runs/:runId` and the `405` of the four-part run-door shapes answer as on `main`.
- **No published schema, type, export or route-ledger row changes.** `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime: patch` with a `**BREAKING**` block and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on both the PR body and the changeset. This is what the card orders, and it matches the diff: one request class changes its answer, and no API surface is added or removed. `Check Changeset` is success on this head. The first-party count of 0 holds on my read: `client.automation.trigger()` builds `trigger/:name`, two segments.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` is empty. The five deviations:

1. **Docblock sentence of `isRunLifecycleWrite` edited.** Accepted. The change made "RUNS that flow" false, and the predicate itself is untouched.
2. **Two test files beyond "its tests".** Accepted. The lifecycle pin asserted the removed behaviour, and the socket file is the only place the mounted host's answer is pinned.
3. **"Before any gate runs anything" measured, not re-placed.** Accepted, and checked in the tree; see ④.
4. **`pnpm lint` narrowed locally.** Accepted. `Lint · ESLint` is success on this head.
5. **Commit trailers.** Not a contract matter.

The dev's out-of-scope note (`client.automation.trigger()` does not encode the name) changes nothing here: a name with `/` was never a served flow name. Nothing is escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

**`automation.ts` (implementing file).** The code agrees with the card, sentence by sentence.

- *"A bare `trigger/:name` and an addressed `trigger/:ns/:name` are served."* Holds. `readAutomationAddress` strips a `trigger` path only at exactly three raw parts with a qualifier in second position, so an addressed call arrives at the arm as two parts and misses `parts.length >= 3`.
- *"Any deeper `POST` is declined."* Holds. A `trigger` path of four or more raw parts is never stripped, so it carries no qualifier and no admission is asked; `bareByNameItem` returns nothing for `trigger` unless the path is two parts. It reaches the decline unchanged.
- *"Before any gate runs anything."* Holds as measured. I read every gate between the address read and the arm. `isRunStateRead` is `GET` only. `isFlowAuthoringWrite`, `isFlowEnablementWrite`, `isFlowActivationWrite` and `isRunLifecycleWrite` each exclude `parts[0] === 'trigger'` on their `POST` arms, or need zero or one part. The two connector predicates need `connectors` first. Only the anonymous floor (`401`) and the service probe (`501`) answer ahead of the decline, as for every path of the domain.
- *"Other verbs are untouched."* Holds.

Attempts to break it:

- A served shape now declined: none found. Bare two-part and addressed three-part calls are served. `trigger/toggle` and `trigger/clone` (two parts) still run their flow.
- Anything still run past the bound: none found. Before this change every `POST trigger/:x/…` returned from the legacy arm, so no arm below it ever served such a path; the decline takes nothing from them.
- A flow named `trigger`: its `POST` run doors (`trigger/runs/:runId/resume|cancel|restore-suspension`) were never reachable, because the legacy arm ran the flow `runs` instead. They are now no route. This is the case the review on PR #32001 told the card to carry.

**`automation-addressed-route.test.ts`.** Holds. It pins the bare depths (four, five, the three run-door shapes), the addressed depths, the `dispatch()` seam, and the CONTROLs for the served shapes and the other verbs. All three pins of card item 3 are present.

**`automation-run-lifecycle-door.test.ts`.** Holds. The flipped pin asserts `handled: false`, no `403`, and neither `execute` nor `cancelRun` called. That is the new contract for this path.

**`automation-every-verb.hono.integration.test.ts`.** Holds. The recording `execute` makes "nothing ran" observable over a socket, and the CONTROL shows the double does run a served call.

Findings:

- **nit** — `automation-addressed-route.test.ts`, the CONTROL "another verb at four segments is the flow `trigger`'s too". It pins `405` with `Allow: POST` on `trigger/runs/r1/resume|cancel`. After the bound, the `POST` that header names is no route. The header comes from `automationRouteAllow` (outside the diff), and card item 2 orders other verbs left untouched. Before the bound that `POST` ran the flow `runs`, so the header was no truer. A follow-up card could drop `POST` from `Allow` when the first part is `trigger`.
- **nit** — `automation.ts`, `isRunLifecycleWrite` docblock. After the corrected sentence, "Gating it would over-block an execution door" now describes a path the door declines. The exclusion is still right: a gate there would answer `403` on a no-route path. Prose only.
- **nit** — the catch-all host's `404` is pinned at the `dispatch()` seam, not over a `createHonoApp` socket. The host's branch is read above and is unchanged by this diff.

No must-fix and no should-fix. Nits alone: the round ends here.
